messages:
Maria: Quick question — auditor_jane asked for evidence showing RBAC delegation changes (who approved role grants) plus KMS decrypt access trace for a commit window (2025-11-20..2025-11-23). Does anyone have the export workflow we should hand to them?

Alex: We have two pieces: RBAC audits (GCP/IAM and internal SSO) and KMS access logs (cloudkms + SIEM). For GCP we can run a query; for Okta we pull the system audit. I can export a signed bundle.

Ben: Auditor wants control mapping to SOC 2 CC6.1 and ISO A.9.2 equivalents — they need change approvals (Jira ticket + approver) + attestation. Include a CSV mapping ticket -> approver -> timestamp.

Claire: Quick clarifying Q — do we include envelope key usage only or full decrypt events with requester identity and invocation context?

auditor_jane: Please include envelope key usage *and* decrypt events. We need requester identity, invocation context (region, IP), and the associated service account or user. Also include the approval ticket for any role grant tied to key access.

Maria: Draft export commands below — adjust for prod retention window and scrub rules: 

```
# GCP KMS decrypt log (Cloud Logging)
gcloud logging read 'resource.type="cloud_kms_crypto_key" protoPayload.methodName="Decrypt" AND timestamp>="2025-11-20T00:00:00Z" AND timestamp<="2025-11-23T23:59:59Z"' --format=json > kms_decrypt_20251120_23.json

# Okta system log for role changes
okta logs -q 'eventType eq "user.role.update" and published gt "2025-11-20T00:00:00Z"' --since 2025-11-20 --until 2025-11-23 > okta_role_changes_20251120_23.json

# Internal RBAC (postgres)
psql -h rbac-db -c "COPY (SELECT actor, target_role, approved_by, ticket_id, changed_at FROM role_changes WHERE changed_at >= '2025-11-20' AND changed_at < '2025-11-24') TO STDOUT WITH CSV HEADER" > rbac_role_changes_20251120_23.csv
```

Alex: After export, push to secure-s3 org bucket with encrypted transfer, then generate manifest: 

```
aws s3 cp kms_decrypt_20251120_23.json s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/2025-11-kms/ --sse aws:kms
aws s3 cp okta_role_changes_20251120_23.json s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/2025-11-okta/ --sse aws:kms
aws s3 cp rbac_role_changes_20251120_23.csv s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/2025-11-rbac/ --sse aws:kms

# manifest (example)
# manifest.csv columns: filename,sha256,uploaded_by,upload_ts
```

Ben: For auditor_jane include a mapping file control_map.csv with columns control_id,artifact_path,explanation. Also zip and sign the bundle (pgp) and drop a presigned link to the auditor ticket. Add a short narrative (2-3 bullets) explaining how each artifact satisfies the control.

auditor_jane: Thanks — can you confirm that the Okta export includes admin approve events and includes user agent/IP? Also we need the narrative tying artifacts to the control objective.

Claire: I'll validate the Okta export contains admin approval events plus user_agent + IP. If any entries are missing we'll annotate them (e.g., missing IPs because of proxy) in the narrative and flag for forensic follow-up. Note: we must redact customer IPs — only internal staff IPs are kept.

DevOpsBot: export-job finished (run id: cj-20260315-42) — artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/2025-11-kms/kms_decrypt_20251120_23.json (sha256: abc123def456...), s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/2025-11-okta/okta_role_changes_20251120_23.json, s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/2025-11-rbac/rbac_role_changes_20251120_23.csv

Maria: Perfect. Ben can you assemble control_map.csv + the 2–3 bullet narrative and ping auditor_jane?

Ben: Will do — target EOD PST. I'll attach the signed zip and add a note about retention window + redaction policy.

Maria: Thanks :thumbsup:
notes: auditor asked specifically for mapping to SOC2/ISO controls, include both logs and approval artifacts, scrub customer IPs, PGP sign before upload
